title: Profits and Gains of Business or Profession

content.overview: Business and professional income is the section 28 profit after deductions for rent, repairs, depreciation, insurance and other expenditure laid out wholly and exclusively for the purpose of the business. Personal expenses, capital expenditure and the enacted disallowances are not deducted. Presumptive computation applies only where that scheme is chosen and the section allows it. The computation is net profit. A business purpose is required for a deduction.

cases.issue: What must a tax levy clearly identify to be valid?

cases.facts: The Court considered treaty benefits, circulars and tax avoidance arguments.
cases.issue: How should a valid tax treaty and administrative circular operate?
cases.ratioDecidendi: A treaty and valid administrative practice must be respected unless displaced by law; legitimate tax planning is not automatically evasion.

cases.name: Union of India v. Mohit Minerals Pvt. Ltd.
cases.facts: The case concerned GST levy and the legal effect of a Council recommendation.
cases.issue: What is the constitutional and statutory force of GST Council recommendations?
cases.ratioDecidendi: GST Council recommendations have persuasive value within the constitutional design but are not automatically binding as primary legislation without statutory implementation.
cases.holding: The Court interpreted the federal GST framework accordingly.
cases.relevance: Use for GST levy, delegated action and constitutional federalism.

enhancement.legalPrinciple: The computation is net profit. A business purpose is required for a deduction.
essentialIngredients: Deduction wholly and exclusively for business
Depreciation instead of the capital cost
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Sections 30 to 36 list specific deductions. Section 37 is the residual business expenditure. Capital expenditure is recovered through depreciation where the asset qualifies. Cash payments above the enacted limit, unpaid statutory dues, and excessive related-party payments are disallowances. Presumptive taxation replaces actual computation only for the eligible business and the declared figure.
examples: Rent of the shop and staff wages are deducted.
The proprietor's household expense is not.
A new machine is depreciated, not deducted in full.
